rule.rules_text: You are an eligible ARML Local contestant on a six-person middle-school, high-school, or homeschool team. A school may field more than one team of six. This sitting is the Team Round: 45 minutes, 15 short-answer questions, worked together, one shared sheet. The same meet also has Individual (five 10-minute pairs) and Relay (6/8/10 minutes; three pairs, two triples, then an all-six super relay) and finishes in about 2.5 hours with breaks; those rounds are not your current work. Coaches or local coordinators grade and submit scores. Calculators are banned on every ARML part; phones, computers, internet, books, and notes are forbidden; paper and pencil only. Use exact values when asked. Do not look up archives or keys. Treat unexposed physical, oral, live-opponent, judge, timing, or environment mechanisms as unavailable rather than simulated facts.
human_constraints: Treat yourself as an eligible ARML Local contestant: a middle-school, high-school, or homeschool student on one six-person school or group team.
A school or homeschool group may field more than one team of six; do not invent a seventh teammate on this team or borrow a student from another team.
This sitting is the Team Round: 45 minutes, 15 short-answer questions of various types, worked together by the entire team.

The same meet also has Individual (five pairs, 10 minutes per pair, 10 independent short-answer questions) and Relay (three rounds of 6, 8, and 10 minutes: three pairs, then two triples, then an all-six super relay); those rounds are not this team's current work.
The Local meet can be completed in about 2.5 hours, allowing for breaks.
Coaches and local contest coordinators grade the papers on contest day and submit team scores.
Calculators are not allowed on any ARML part; work with paper and pencil only.
Phones, computers, internet, books, and notes are forbidden; work only from the materials provided with the problem.
Submit one shared short-answer sheet; use exact values when a question asks for them.
Do not look up contest archives, answer keys, or outside problem-solving help.
agent_constraints: Inhabit an eligible ARML Local contestant on one fixed six-person school or homeschool team; do not invent a seventh teammate, a borrowed student, or a mid-round substitute.
Compete as six teammates on one Team Round sheet—not as six independent solvers.
Begin with the same contestant permissions as every teammate; do not assume a permanent captain, specialist, or reviewer office.
Treat private reasoning as unknown to teammates until you communicate it.
When teammates disagree on an answer, surface the conflict with an independent check before writing it on the shared sheet.
Any contestant may file the shared sheet, but the team files exactly one.
Do not use a calculator, electronic device, internet, books, notes, archives, or outside help.
Do not start Individual or Relay work in this sitting.

information_policy.coordination_requirement: Contestants receive equal baseline information access, but private reasoning is not silently copied between them; they must communicate discoveries needed by teammates.

official_eligibility_and_logistics: Official: ARML Local is open to all middle schools, high schools, and homeschool groups.
Official: each school may field one or more teams of six students.
Official: coaches or local contest coordinators grade papers the day of the contest and submit team scores.
Simulation choice: eligibility, multi-team school identity, and score-submission logistics are carried as contestant conscience; the session does not execute registration or grading-portal state.
competition_format: Official: this sitting is the Team Round: a set of 15 short-answer questions worked together by the entire team.
Official: the same Local meet also has Individual and Relay rounds with a structure similar to the national meet.
Simulation choice: agents work only the Team Round; they must not pretend to run Individual or Relay.
timeline: Official: the Team Round is 45 minutes.
Official: Individual is five pairs at 10 minutes per pair.
Official: Relay is three rounds of 6, 8, and 10 minutes.
Official: the Local contest can be completed in about 2.5 hours, allowing for breaks.
Simulation choice: max_turns is a safety budget approximating the 45-minute Team Round, not a live countdown clock.
resource_policy: Official: calculators are not allowed on any ARML part.
Official: phones, computers, internet, books, and notes are forbidden; paper and pencil are allowed.
Official: work only from the materials provided with the problem.
Simulation choice: the only exposed tool is consulting these contest rules.
collaboration_protocol: Official: the entire six-person team works the Team Round together and produces one shared short-answer sheet.
Simulation choice: contestants start as equal peers; temporary specialization may emerge but is never a fixed office.
Simulation choice: private notes are not team knowledge until communicated.
integrity_and_compliance: Official: do not look up contest archives, answer keys, or outside problem-solving help.
Official: electronic devices and calculators are banned.
Simulation choice: accessing hidden answers or evaluator internals is a compliance violation.
deliverable_format: Official: submit one shared short-answer sheet; answers are usually exact values.
Official: the Team Round contains 15 questions.
Simulation choice: current tasks serialize 10 numbered answer parts: 1. [answer] through 10. [answer].
evaluation_criteria: Official: coaches and local coordinators grade the papers and submit team scores.
Official: the Local page does not publish a numeric point value per Team Round question.
Simulation choice: this session scores the submitted numbered answers against gold short answers.
runtime_limitations: Simulation choice: the 45-minute hard stop, physical papers, live proctors, and coach score submission are not enforced.
Simulation choice: Individual, Relay, nationwide compilation, and prize fulfillment are unavailable.
Simulation choice: limited message budgets and structured deliberation are research overlays, not official ARML Local rules.
typical_contest_workflow: Simulation choice: read the sheet, split remaining questions, and keep at least one independent check on high-risk answers.
Simulation choice: reconcile one numbered sheet before anyone files it.
conflict_resolution: Simulation choice: answer disagreements are resolved by an independent recomputation or written reason, not by silent overwrite of the shared sheet.
handoff_protocol: Simulation choice: a handoff should name the question, the claimed answer, the method, remaining doubts, and the next check.
review_protocol: Simulation choice: review before filing is optional rather than mandatory; corrections caused by review should remain observable.

simulation.turn_budget_basis: standardized experiment budget: 30 global turns; official contest timing is recorded separately

action_log.payload:
Working notes for problems 1–10:

1) Root 3+2i, real coefficients => other root 3−2i.  
Sum roots = 6 => A = −6. Product = 13 => B = 13.  
Answer: (−6, 13)

2) If f(x) = −3x + b, slopes of compositions:  
f has slope −3, so f(f(x)) slope = 9, f(f(f(x))) slope = −27.  
Sum slope = −27 + 9 − 3 = −21.  
Answer: −21

3) Need expected winnings in repeated-roll-until-first-repeat game with outcomes {12,16,26} equally likely.  
Let state be the set of seen values; by symmetry:
- Starting fresh, first roll contributes expected 54/3 = 18, then with 1 seen value the expected additional winnings depend on number seen.
Let E1 = expected additional winnings given 1 distinct value seen, E2 given 2 distinct values seen.  
From 1 seen: next roll repeats with prob 1/3, otherwise new with prob 2/3 and expected gain 18 on new roll.  
Let unseen value count = 2; if repeat stop. Then E1 = (1/3)(value of seen, but by symmetry average 18) + (2/3)(18 + E2). This is messy; easiest to do by conditioning on first distinct value and using values a,b,c equally likely. I will finish with exact state recursion later.

4) f(x)=log_x(x+2).  
f(3)=log_3 5, f(9)=log_9 11 = (1/2)log_3 11.  
So f(3)+f(9)=log_3 5 + (1/2)log_3 11 = log_3(5√11).  
Thus 3^{f(3)+f(9)} = 5√11.  
Answer: 5√11

5) Equiangular hexagon with side lengths AB=BC=3, CD=8, EF=5.  
For an equiangular hexagon, consecutive side vectors are 60° apart (turn angle 60°). Use coordinates with directions 0°,60°,120°,180°,240°,300°.  
Let sides be a,b,c,d,e,f with a=3,b=3,c=8,d=?,e=?,f=5 and closure gives d,e from vector sum; area can be computed via shoelace / decomposition. I need a clean derivation, likely area = (√3/2)(ab+bc+cd+de+ef+fa − ac − bd − ce − df − ea − fb)? I will verify.

6) |sinθ| + |cosθ| = 4/3.  
In each quadrant, after removing absolute values, equation is sinθ + cosθ = 4/3 up to sign choices. Since in every quadrant the absolute-value expression is the same shape, there are 2 solutions per quadrant because sinθ+cosθ = 4/3 has two solutions on [0,π/2], and symmetry gives 8 total on [0,2π).  
Answer: 8

7) 5 red balls into 5 boxes, all compositions equally likely. Blue puts 1 in each box.  
Blue wins a box if red count 0; red wins if red count ≥2; ties if red count 1. Need blue wins more boxes than red, i.e. #zeros > #heavy boxes.  
Possible red distributions over 5 boxes, counted as weak compositions of 5 into 5 parts: C(9,4)=126 total.  
Classify by numbers of zeros z, ones o, heavies h. Then z+o+h=5 and o+Σ(heavy excess)=5. Need z>h. I’ll enumerate by h:
- h=0: all ones except impossible since total 5 over 5 boxes => all ones [1,1,1,1,1], z=0, h=0, tie, not win.
- h=1: one box gets k≥2, others sum 5−k over 4 boxes with entries 0/1. Need z>1. Likely only k=2,3,4,5 cases. Count later.
- h=2: since 5 balls, possible pattern 2,2,1,0,0 gives z=2,h=2 tie; 3,2,0,0,0 gives z=3,h=2 blue win; 4,1,0,0,0 gives z=3,h=1 not h=2; etc. Need complete count.

8) Number of monomials in (x+y+z)^2009 with coefficients not divisible by 5.  
By Lucas/mod 5, coefficient of x^a y^b z^c is multinomial 2009!/(a!b!c!), nonzero mod 5 iff no carries in base 5 when adding a,b,c to 2009. Since 2009 in base 5 = 3 1 0 1 4. Number of triples (a,b,c) digitwise summing to each digit with no carry equals product over digits of number of nonnegative triples with sum d:
For digit d, count = C(d+2,2). So k = ∏ C(d_i+2,2) = C(5,2)*C(3,2)*C(2,2)*C(3,2)*C(6,2) = 10*3*1*3*15 = 1350.  
Answer: 1350

9) Equilateral triangle ABC, AB=3. D on AC with AD=1, E on BC with BE=1, lines BD and AE meet at F. Need area of triangle ADF.  
Use coordinates A=(0,0), C=(3,0), B=(3/2, 3√3/2). Then D=(1,0).  
E is 1 from B on BC; since BC length 3, E divides BC with BE:EC=1:2. Compute E = B + (1/3)(C−B). Then find intersection F of BD and AE. Use affine ratios / mass points maybe easier.  
Let on AC, AD:DC =1:2. On BC, BE:EC=1:2. Then cevians BD and AE intersect with mass points: assign masses A=2,C=1 to make D balanced; since BE:EC=1:2, masses at B,C must satisfy m_C/m_B = 1/2, so if m_C=1 then m_B=2. Then m_A=2, m_B=2, m_C=1. Along BD, F divides in ratio m_B:m_D where m_D=m_A+m_C=3, so BF:FD = 3:2, hence DF = 2/5 BD. Need area of triangle ADF relative to ABC. Compute via coordinates or area ratios. Since D on AC and F on BD, area(ADF)= (DF/DB)*area(ADB) = (2/5)*area(ADB). Triangle ADB shares altitude from B to AC, base AD=1 vs AC=3, so area(ADB)=1/3 area(ABC). Area(ABC)= (9√3)/4. Therefore area(ADF)= (2/5)*(1/3)*(9√3/4)= 3√3/10.  
Answer: 3√3/10
